content.title: About
content.content: Curry sauce is a fragrant blend of tomatoes, cream, spices and herbs typical of Indian cuisine. It has a rich, mildly spicy flavor with notes of coriander, turmeric, ginger and garlic. Suitable for meat, fish, vegetables and rice dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Curry sauce originated in the United Kingdom in the 19th century as a Western adaptation of Indian dishes.
There are many variants – red, yellow, green – each distinguished by a different spice mix.
Traditional Indian curries often use coconut milk, while Western versions frequently rely on dairy cream.
Turmeric gives the sauce its bright yellow colour and provides antioxidant properties.
Curry sauce is a staple in fast‑food dishes such as curry‑rice and curry‑noodles.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Spices like turmeric and coriander contain antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ginger and garlic stimulate gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory properties
items.content: Curcumin, the active component of turmeric, is known for its anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Ingredients in curry sauce often provide B6 and B12 vitamins, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Garlic and spices may help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turmeric, coriander, ginger or garlic.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared curry sauce can contain a notable amount of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot versions may irritate the stomach of those with sensitive digestive systems.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Commercial varieties sometimes add sugar for balance, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add curry sauce to sautéed meat, chicken, fish or vegetables, use it as a base for soups, or as a topping for casseroles. It also pairs well with rice, couscous or noodles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store curry sauce in the refrigerator in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 5–7 days. It can be frozen for up to 3 months, though texture may change.
